title: Proxy-holdback tenant evacuation and elastic failover for cross-region KV mismatch
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Customers on hosted and dedicated fleets experienced elevated 5xx rates during a cross-region pair failover when a subset of tenants saw stale KV snapshot references. This ticket implements a conservative proxy-holdback strategy that prevents in-flight traffic from flipping to a region with known KV index drift, plus an elastic controlled evacuation that stages tenant movement with health-verification gates.
background: At 2025-02-08 we observed repeated small windows where the regional leader election completed but the downstream KV index reconciler lagged for ~5-20s for a subset of tenant namespaces. Affected tenants saw elevated model decode errors and token errors when routed to the target region. Temporary mitigations (short circuit to older model variant) reduced surface area but caused customer confusion and billing spikes. We need a reproducible, low-risk evacuation flow that keeps customers online and minimizes tail-error exposure.
acceptance_criteria: Traffic routing layer supports 'proxy-holdback' flag per-tenant that temporarily prevents switch to target region until KV health check passes
Evacuation orchestration stages tenants in batches (configurable batch size) with per-batch success/failure thresholds
End-to-end test harness simulates KV desync and verifies no more than 0.1% increase in 5xx for evacuated tenants during rollout
Runbook documentation updated with step-by-step operator commands and Slack/PagerDuty play channels
Customer-facing postmortem template drafted for support and CSM teams
mitigation_playbook: Stage 0: Detect — metric spike alert triggers when tenant 5xx rate or KV reconciliation lag > 3s for 3 consecutive eval windows
Stage 1: Quarantine — set proxy-holdback=true for impacted tenant IDs via routing API; this pins requests to source region until health checks clear
Stage 2: Snapshot validation — run KV snapshot compare job (fast diff) between source and target; if diffs exist, block automated switchover
Stage 3: Controlled Evacuation — start batch 1 (default 5 tenants) using evacuation API; each tenant batch must pass 2 minutes of golden-path tests and KV-read checks before proceeding
Stage 4: Fallback & rollback — if batch failure rate > 1% or error pattern correlates to KV read failures, abort and revert batches; notify customers and run hotfix path
Stage 5: Post-evac monitoring — increase sampling telemetry and hold SLA buffer for 60 minutes after final batch

actions_taken: Added feature flag 'proxy_holdback_v1' to routing-control service
Instrumented KV reconciler to expose fast-diff API for per-tenant snapshot comparison
Implemented batch evacuation controller with circuit breaker and health gates
Created temporary dashboard for support with per-tenant holdback state and reconciliation status
Notified top 5 impacted customers and offered guided evacuation window
rollback_plan: If canary or initial batches show >1% spike in 5xx or any increase in unknown token decode errors, revert routing-control to previous stable config (disable proxy_holdback flag and abort evacuation). Revert is fast (API toggle) but may leave tenants routed to degraded target region; if revert fails, perform manual traffic rehome to designated warm standby region and open incident escalation to SRE oncall.
